title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are not biased towards texture: Revisiting feature re

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The caption defines all tabulated values as relative accuracy (suppression accuracy divided by original accuracy), but the 'Original' column contains absolute accuracies (e.g., Humans 0.969, ResNet50-standard 0.954). If the caption were taken literally, the Original column would be 1.000 for every row.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.2, Remote Sensing paragraph and Figure 4 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says 'Figure 4g–i reports suppression curves for five very-high-resolution RGB datasets: UCMerced [61], RSD46-WHU [62], DeepGlobe [63], PatternNet [64], and AID [65].' The Figure 4 caption/subfigures instead list AID, EuroSAT, NWPU, RESISC45, and UC Merced. The cited RSD46-WHU, DeepGlobe and PatternNet references do not correspond to the datasets shown.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.2, Medical Imaging paragraph and Figure 4d–f
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says 'Figure 4d–f summarizes results on five MedMNIST-v2 datasets' and then discusses RetinaMNIST and ChestMNIST, but the figure list contains BloodMNIST, BreastMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, and PathMNIST only. RetinaMNIST and ChestMNIST are not among the five datasets shown.

The text says 'The five suppression conditions of one image were split across groups of five participants to ensure balanced coverage. Only twenty participants completed the study...' Five groups of five participants would require 25 participants, not 20. The allocation/coverage of the five conditions across 20 participants is inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 Param ID A vs Section 5.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 lists Bilateral Filter parameter A as d=11, while Section 5.1 states 'bilateral filtering with d=12, σ_color=170 and σ_space=75'. The kernel diameter for the same method is given inconsistently.

The dataset is described as 'constructed by selecting 50 images per category from the ImageNet validation set', which would produce a balanced set (ImageNet validation has 50 images per class). The next sentence claims 'Categories with fewer confident predictions were left as is, leading to class imbalance' without explaining how imbalance can arise from this procedure or what 'fewer confident predictions' refers to at dataset construction time.

The text says 'Model predictions were determined using the argmax class across all subclasses without thresholding... complementary results using argmax to define class predictions are reported in the supplemental material'. Since the primary procedure already uses argmax, the 'complementary' results using the same argmax rule cannot be a distinct analysis; the sentence is internally contradictory.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 4 axes and Section 5.2 normalization description
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The figure axes are labeled 'Accuracy (Relative to No Suppression)', but the text states 'Chance-level accuracies were rescaled to zero and baseline accuracies to one'. This is not the same as the simple ratio used in Figure 3/Table 3; the label can mislead readers about the reported quantity.

The paper describes a behavioral study with 20 human participants, brief exposure, attention checks, etc., but does not report ethics approval/IRB review or informed consent. Human-subjects research requires such statements.

The text states Patch Rotation 'may partially disrupt both shape and local texture cues due to edge discontinuities... Both transformations primarily disrupt shape but can unintentionally affect texture, complicating a clean feature separation.' However, Table 2 reports Texture=1.000, LV=1.000, HFE=1.000 for both Patch Shuffle and Patch Rotation, and Section 4.1 later concludes 'These transformations preserve texture'. The prose and quantitative validation are inconsistent.
